{{Short description|Swiss mathematician, physicist and diver (1934–2022)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2024}}
[[Image:Hannes Keller by Esther Keller.jpg|thumb|Hannes Keller]]
'''Hannes Keller''' (20 September 1934 – {{Death date and age|2022|12|1|1934|9|20|df=y}}) was a Swiss physicist, mathematician, [[deep diving]] pioneer, and entrepreneur. In 1962, he reached a depth of {{convert|1000|ft|m}} in open ocean.<ref name=spums1999>{{cite journal |author1=Wendling, J |author2=Nussberger, P |author3=Schenk, B |title=Milestones of the deep diving research laboratory Zurich. |journal=South Pacific Underwater Medicine Society Journal |volume=29 |issue=2 |year=1999 |issn=0813-1988 |oclc=16986801 |url=http://archive.rubicon-foundation.org/6003 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120709074212/http://archive.rubicon-foundation.org/6003 |url-status=usurped |archive-date=July 9, 2012 |access-date=2008-09-12 }}</ref><ref>Eaton, Bernard (2002) [http://www.divernet.com/cgi-bin/articles.pl?id=2600&sc=1040&ac=d&an=2600:The+Atlantis+affair... The Atlantis affair]{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}, ''Diver'' magazine, December 2002</ref><ref>Tillman, Thomas (1999) [http://www.divinghistory.com/kellerdive.htm The Keller Dive] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071224193915/http://divinghistory.com/kellerdive.htm |date=2007-12-24 }}</ref>
In the 1970s through the 1980s, Keller made himself a name as an entrepreneur in the [[Information technology|IT]] industry.<ref name=HKweb>{{cite web |url=http://hanneskeller.com/index.php?template=2biografie&l=english |author=hanneskeller.com |publisher=hanneskeller.com |title=Hannes Keller Biography |access-date=2008-09-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110817162508/http://hanneskeller.com/index.php?template=2biografie&l=english |archive-date=2011-08-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Keller was also an amateur [[european classical music|classical]] [[pianist]] who produced two [[compact disc|CD]]s and occasionally performed for audiences of up to 2000 people.<ref name=HKweb/><ref name=HKconcert>{{cite web |url=http://hanneskeller.com/index.php?template=2music&l=english |author=hanneskeller.com |publisher=hanneskeller.com |title=Hannes Keller In Concert |access-date=2008-09-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110817162830/http://hanneskeller.com/index.php?template=2music&l=english |archive-date=2011-08-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=perform>{{cite web |url=http://www.camasb.org/archives/1990-2k.shtml |title=December 5, 1993; American Youth Symphony; Zubin Mehta, Conductor; Theo Lieven & Hannes Keller, Pianos at the Arlington Theatre |author=Community Arts Music Association |year=1993 |access-date=2008-09-12 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080704174342/http://www.camasb.org/archives/1990-2k.shtml |archive-date=July 4, 2008 }}</ref>

==Deep diving==
[[Image:Keller US NEDU.jpg|thumb|Keller donning diving dress at the [[United States Navy Experimental Diving Unit]]<ref name=auas>{{cite journal |title=Hannes Keller and His Secret Mixtures |publisher=Oceanaut Press |journal=The History of Oil Field Diving |volume=Chapter 8 |author=Swann, C |year=2007 |pages=105–113 |url=http://www.auas-nogi.org/hist_oil_field_keller.pdf |access-date=2008-09-12 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081120062842/http://www.auas-nogi.org/hist_oil_field_keller.pdf |archive-date=2008-11-20 }}</ref>]]

Keller was born in [[Winterthur]], Switzerland. He studied [[philosophy]], [[mathematics]], and [[theoretical physics]] at the [[University of Zurich]]. He became interested in deep diving and developed tables for mixed-gas decompression, supported by [[Albert A. Bühlmann]] who suggested suitable gases.<ref name=spums1999/><ref name=HKweb/> Keller successfully tested his idea in [[Lake Zurich]], where he reached a depth of {{convert|400|ft|m}}, and [[Lake Maggiore]], where he reached a depth of {{convert|728|ft|m}}.<ref name=LifeMag1961>{{cite magazine |title=Deepest dive ever made, Hannes Keller Ken MacLeish in Lake Maggiore to 728 feet. |magazine=[[Life (magazine)|Life magazine]] |date=1961-08-04 |page=66}}</ref> On 3 December 1962,<ref name=DDAAG1995>{{cite book|title=Deep Diving: An Advanced Guide To Physiology, Procedures And Systems|year=1995|publisher=Aqua Quest Publications|isbn=0922769311|pages=60ff|author=Bret Gilliam|author2=Robert Von Maier |author3=Darren Webb }}</ref> he set a new world record when he reached a depth of {{convert|1000|ft|m}} off the coast of [[Santa Catalina Island, California]], together with [[Peter Small (diver)|Peter Small]].<ref name=auas/><ref name=hdsV12>{{cite journal |title=Towards the Limits of the Continental Shelf |author=Keller, H |journal=Historical Diver Magazine |publisher=The Historical Diving Society USA, Inc. |volume=12 |issue=3 |year=2004 |url=http://www.hds.org/back_issues.html#summer04 |access-date=2008-09-12 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080920074937/http://www.hds.org/back_issues.html#summer04 |archive-date=2008-09-20 }}</ref> This major achievement was overshadowed by the tragic end of the mission: Keller was lucky to survive while Peter Small and Chris Whittaker, a young [[UCLA]] student and supporting diver, lost their lives.<ref name=Eaton>{{cite journal |author=Eaton, B |title=The Atlantis affair |journal=South Pacific Underwater Medicine Society Journal Reprinted from Diver, December 2002: 85–87 |volume=33 |issue=4 |year=2003 |url=http://archive.rubicon-foundation.org/8128 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130415175335/http://archive.rubicon-foundation.org/8128 |url-status=usurped |archive-date=April 15, 2013 |access-date=2009-08-07 }}</ref>

In the following years, [[navy|navies]] and hospitals bought [[decompression chamber]]s constructed by Keller.

==Career after diving==
In the 1970s, Keller sold his own line of computers and in the 1980s became a leading vendor of [[IBM PC]]s in Switzerland.<ref name=HKweb/> He developed a series of software products (Witchpen, Ways for Windows, and Wizardmaker) which provided automatic [[spell checker|spell checking]], literal [[machine translation]], and [[Macro (computer science)|macro]] recording.

Keller used to run Visipix<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.visipix.com|title=Visipix|website=www.visipix.com}}</ref> the largest fine art and photo museum online with 1.3 million exhibits, all with free copyrights for any use.<ref name=HKweb/>

After 2005, Keller was a full-time artist.<ref name=HKweb/>

In 2009, Keller joined the advisory board for the United States Historical Diving Society.<ref name=HDS2009>{{cite journal |year=2009 |title=HDSUSA Welcomes Hannes Keller to the advisory board |journal=The Journal of Diving History |volume=17 |number=58 |pages=4  |publisher=Historical Diving Society USA, Inc. }}</ref><!-- |issue=1 removed (crashed template) -->

Keller died on 1 December 2022 in [[Niederglatt]], Switzerland, at the age of 88.<ref>Phil Davison: [https://www.washingtonpost.com/obituaries/2022/12/25/hannes-keller-dive-sea-dies/ ''Hannes Keller, deep diver who pioneered breathing gas mix, dies at 88.''] In: ''Washington Post'', 25 December 2022.</ref>
